saints.name: St. John Joseph of the Cross
saints.title: Priest, Franciscan
saints.shortBlurb: A Franciscan of the Alcantarine reform who carried stones for his brethren and was known for miracles and prophecy…
biography: Born Carlo Gaetano Calosirto on the island of Ischia on 15 August 1654, John Joseph entered the Friars Minor at Naples before he was sixteen, the first Italian to join the Alcantarine reform founded in Spain by St. Peter of Alcántara, and took the name by which he is known.

In 1674 he was sent to found a friary at Piedimonte and labored at its building with his own hands. Ordained priest much against his will, he chose as superior the lowliest offices, slept but three hours a night, and never tasted wine.

When the Italian Alcantarines were formed into a separate province in 1702, he was made their vicar provincial and guided the fragile branch through its first trials. People of every rank were brought to him for healing, yet he bade those he cured take some medicine, that the cure might be ascribed to nature and not to him.

He died at Naples on 5 March, worn out by a life of austerity. Beatified by Pope Pius VI in 1789 and canonized by Pope Gregory XVI in 1839, he is venerated as patron of Ischia, where a chapel in the Aragonese Castle bears his name.
saints.knownFor: Restoring strict observance among the Italian Franciscans.
